approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from a population ranked by real observed scores. A count-fingerprint Gaussian model guides a two-batch decision: it values the first batch together with the second batch it would choose after seeing those outcomes. It also constructs and saves four possible mutations of each candidate first-batch source. These bank products become second-batch options only when their actual or hypothetical source survives the same population rule. The Parent applies a source-relative sulfur-signature rejection to ordinary offspring, to bank construction, and again when a saved bank product is materialized. Every real fit and breeding update uses only accepted observations from the current session.
approach.novelty: Remove sulfur rejection throughout this existing bank composition while retaining its exact passive classifier and source-survival requirement. This lets otherwise admissible products with positive sulfur-signature excess enter ordinary pools and saved future support, where the existing predictive policy can choose them. The earlier removal tested only the ordinary-pool gate on the formal Anchor; this test covers the bank's additional construction and materialization consumers. The parallel bank control removes source-survival eligibility, whereas this Child preserves it. The question is whether the earlier removal's total endpoint sign transfers to this particular host.

observed_bottleneck: The code Parent n-aedff97c8e9f excludes otherwise valid novel options through an unpriced sulfur consumer inside its confirmed contingent-bank mechanism. Its complete Search mean is 0.5602580014730827 (population SD 0.008094049678685718), with +0.009650271640556984 versus its own code Parent but -0.04677231473804836 versus formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de. The bank increased complete 420-window best-progress from 0.023371662586468025 to 0.02430725541129775 and made 784 bank purchases, while 127 windows and 60 committed pairs remained flat. The present raw Search audit recomputed every classifier receipt: 255 of 69,855 ordinary gate opportunities and 59 of 11,661 bank gate opportunities were rejected; the bank made 11,760 fixed mutation calls. These restrictions can change pool refill, future support and later paid search, but their conditional value is unknown. The exact-Anchor removal n-f28be8ac3d12 gained +0.006772407762991002 with five favorable, seven adverse and three tied cells, reduced late progress, and no positive-excess final-winner ancestry. It motivates noninferiority here without establishing transfer or sulfur mediation. Historical additions n-1744a1494180 and n-93cd9a000278 keep their different reference, timing and host conditions. Evidence and source hashes are recorded in policy/scratch/r0079-03-improve-L01/plan/parent-exposure-audit.json and evidence-review.json.

literature_review.conclusion: The supplied Search Policy review and exact internal-evidence adoption support this bounded conditional contribution test. Reuse the recorded review without claiming a new search or a borrowed paper element. Preserve prior favorable and adverse results, the negative formal-Anchor gap and absent positive-D winner mediation; the earlier removal motivates only the pre-registered noninferiority prediction. No external source is used to license broader scope or forecast a positive endpoint.
literature_review.internal_evidence_reason: Use exactly the frozen review's portfolio-position4 internal-evidence basis, recorded in policy/scratch/search_policy-74d2dea100a9/literature-adoptions.json. The complete bank Parent implements and exposes ordinary and bank sulfur enforcement, and the original exact-Anchor removal already establishes a host-specific total contrast. This ticket tests the same admission principle's whole active consumer on the different bank composition; no external mechanism, model, dependency or performance guarantee is introduced. The source-survival/rollout literature adoption belongs to position1 and is not adopted by this Child.

hypothesis: Remove m-93cd9a000278 active rejection at all three existing consumers on n-aedff97c8e9f: ordinary fresh-pool admission, pre-outcome contingent-bank mutation admission, and saved-bank materialization certification. Preserve the exact sulfur envelope, exact local-signature multiplicities and D=sum_h max(C_candidate(h)-R(h),0). For ordinary offspring R is the per-signature maximum over the original scored generating parents, including both original crossover sources through any finishing mutation and the original source through multistep mutation. For bank construction R is the exact linked possible-A source graph; at actual materialization it is that same saved source after real acceptance and top64 survival. A classifier decision of reject becomes passive evidence only; no positive-D reject, skip or raise remains. All other eligibility, identity, support, modeling, policy and survival laws stay active. The causal path is positive-D admission -> changed pool/refill or saved support and its existing conditional valuation -> possible changed real purchases and descendants -> the complete paired total endpoint effect. Direct positive-D purchases need not explain any gain; the experiment does not identify a mediator.

finding_summary.headline: Sulfur-gate removal executed, but noninferiority failed on the bank host
finding_summary.insights:
The earlier favorable removal result does not transfer to this bank composition on the issued Search panel. The signed conclusion is descriptive and conditional on these three seeds. This settles the registered conditional contribution question, while leaving the bank approach and the usefulness of other chemical-admission designs open. It does not price the ordinary and bank consumers independently or establish an interaction coefficient. Newly admitted sulfur-excess lineages can be locally useful even though total removal loses: 31 direct purchases beat their real source, 67 fell below it and 10 tied; 14 increased the incumbent, with total recorded increments 0.467175. 90 survived immediately, 71 were later used as ordinary breeders, and 44 later supplied materialized bank products. Purchased ancestry is a witnessed search path, not identification of sulfur chemistry as the mediator of the total score difference. Pool stopping, support, valuation and subsequent histories change together.

The method still spends many paid decisions without progress: 102 of 210 second batches and 59 committed pairs were flat, and 2,090 of 2,175 late purchases added no incumbent gain. 86 second batches had positive modeled gain but no realized gain. The Parent's mean modeled B gain was 0.00931362 against realized gain 0.01221134. The Child's modeled versus realized B gain was 0.01246942 versus 0.01131674; the pooled descriptive rank correlation was -0.093. These changing-state comparisons show a mismatch between modeled and realized progress on the selected stream. They do not identify ranking failure on unpurchased alternatives or a unique cause of the endpoint loss. A different valuation or ranking model is a method class that could address this limitation; this removal does not test its benefit.

The molecular report shows constitutional variety rather than complete scaffold collapse: generic scaffold counts were 1,119 versus 1,109, with within-session similarity 0.30668 versus 0.30947. Sulfur-bearing output totals were similar, but non-oxygen sulfur multiple-bond drawings increased from 196 to 652. Attachment irregularities and size tails remain, and 2,100 Child products have potential unassigned tetrahedral centres with no explicit configurations. Local-environment-aware proposal operators, coherent scaffold/ring replacements and configuration-aware graph edits address those observed representation and proposal gaps; none is established here as a score improvement or a universal chemical filter.
finding_summary.results:
All 1,582 positive-excess ordinary opportunities entered the pools, and all 282 positive-excess bank opportunities acquired a product or source-alias link. The Parent rejected 255 ordinary and 59 bank opportunities on its own histories. 169 positive-excess saved products passed materialization with their original source witnesses. The 12 exposed sessions matched through the first intended admission difference; 3 unexposed sessions reproduced completely. 2,349 of 4,350 paid positions changed across 11 sessions. 108 direct positive-excess products were purchased, and 422 further purchases carried that ancestry without a new excess at their own admission. 2 final winners had positive-excess ancestry.

Across all 420 adjacent windows, mean realized best-progress changed from 0.02430726 to 0.02407399; flat windows changed from 127 to 128. Mean committed first-batch gain changed from 0.01248511 to 0.01322516, second-batch gain from 0.01221134 to 0.01131674, and pair gain from 0.02469645 to 0.02454189. Flat committed pairs changed from 60 to 59. Late-purchase incumbent gain changed from 1.777269 to 1.116661. All 110,880 planned outcome scenarios and 210 real recourse decisions preserved the source-survival rule, saved conditional law and ordered choices in replay.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.56025800 to 0.55585544, a paired change of -0.00440256. The three seed-macro changes were -0.01534619, 0.00346007, -0.00132156; 4 task/seed endpoints improved, 6 declined and 5 tied. The complete exposed result crosses the registered strict -0.002 noninferiority boundary. The removal executed correctly; its transported noninferiority prediction is refuted. Under the registered signed rule, retaining the gate has positive conditional total endpoint contribution on this bank host. The separate formal-Anchor gap is -0.05117487; its sitagliptin task-regression flag is adverse. All 15 sessions completed with no failed commitment, fallback, invalid or duplicate evaluator submission.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich amide, amine and carbonyl heterocycle families retain unusual attachments, compressed rings and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: This assessment covers n-c5b75b768886 and actual code Parent n-aedff97c8e9f on all five objectives and frozen Search seeds 0, 1 and 2. context.comparison separately records child_complete=true and paired_complete=true. All 15 Child and 15 published Parent trajectory paths exist; every paired session has the same ten initial identities and scores. Each side contains 4,350 accepted optimizer products, excluding initial observations. These trajectories do not enumerate unpurchased internal candidates. The output is predominantly medium-sized, branched aromatic and heteroaromatic chemistry: indole-like aryl amides or esters, linked nitrogen-rich carbonyl heterocycles, aryl/amine frameworks, ethers, halogens and sulfur substituents. Saturated and unsaturated fused rings, expanded heterocycles and occasional repeated large assemblies also occur. Both sides have a median of 30 heavy atoms and four perceived rings; median aromatic-ring counts are two in the Child and three in the Parent. Ring-bearing products number 4,174 versus 4,181, and aromatic-atom-bearing products 4,127 versus 4,063. The digest ring-closure and aromatic-atom counters are presence rates, consistent with abundant ring chemistry; they are not fractions of atoms or proofs of aromatic stability. There are 1,815 nonempty typed Murcko scaffolds and 1,119 generic scaffolds in the Child versus 1,761 and 1,109 in the Parent. Mean within-session Morgan Tanimoto among products with more than five heavy atoms is 0.3066827363054243 versus 0.3094694511553078. This supports substantial constitutional variation with recurrent local families, not complete collapse; the figures do not establish useful diversity. Both sides span one to 120 heavy atoms. Small products with at most five heavy atoms number 170 versus 162, and products with at least 50 number 182 versus 183. Sulfur-bearing product totals are similar, 1,807 versus 1,815, while products containing a sulfur double bond to a non-oxygen atom number 652 versus 196. Carbon-sulfur triple-bond drawings occur in four Child products and none in the Parent. This is a change in observed attachment chemistry, not evidence that sulfur-containing molecules as a class are undesirable or that sulfur mediated any score difference. N-halogen-bearing products number 676 versus 763, O-halogen 72 versus 58, peroxide 75 versus 59, and N-S single-bond-bearing products 895 versus 964; the differences are mixed. Products containing a perceived ring of at most four atoms with an aromatic or multiple ring bond number 824 versus 898; that descriptor flags geometries for review rather than measuring strain. Neither side contains explicit atom or bond stereochemistry or assigned tetrahedral centres. At least one unassigned potential tetrahedral centre occurs in 2,100 Child products versus 2,300 Parent products. Rich rings, aromatic groups and accessible aliphatic amines are demonstrated capabilities. Consistent ordinary attachment environments, configuration-resolved structures, coherent size changes and conservative ring closures remain gaps. All graph descriptors use identical RDKit 2023.09.6 definitions on both sides and retain repeated identities across sessions. Synthetic plausibility is a structural judgement; no route, stability, protonation state, efficacy, toxicity, activation or component contribution is established. No unseen optimal pharmacophore or guaranteed benefit from removing a flagged group is inferred. Methods and full derived counts are in policy/scratch/r0079-03-improve-L01/molecular/aggregate.json. Original absolute paths, byte-identical run-local Child copies and source hashes are in policy/scratch/r0079-03-improve-L01/molecular/provenance.json. Published Parent Search trajectories are the comparison authority. No requested paths or paired molecular comparisons are missing; no other molecular comparator is asserted.

per_task.generated_character: The enriched family consists of compact indole-like fused aromatic systems carrying an aryl amide or ester, with methoxy, methyl, halomethyl, amino and sulfur substitutions. Median size is 25 heavy atoms and three rings on both sides; the Child range is one to 35 heavy atoms, and 821/870 products contain aromatic atoms. Seed 0 favors an indole carboxylate ester linked to a fluoromethyl-substituted pyridyl ring, whereas its Parent favored an N-sulfanyl aryl amide. Seed 1 retains the same N-amino/N-halo aryl-amide best as the Parent; seed 2 favors an N-chloro amide and an N-fluorinated indole-like nitrogen. Thus the broad aromatic/polar arrangement persists while attachments change. The conventional aryl ester and amide building blocks are recognizable, but many whole molecules have questionable attachment chemistry. liabilities: N-halogen bonds occur in 391/870 Child products versus 377 in the Parent; the equal-scoring N-fluoro and N-bromo examples show that stored score does not settle attachment plausibility.

Sulfur double bonds to non-oxygen atoms occur in 50 products versus 18, and two Child products contain a carbon-sulfur triple-bond drawing. Local sulfur bonding needs review rather than a blanket sulfur judgement.
No atom or bond stereo is encoded. Sixty-one Child products versus 64 Parent products have an unassigned potential tetrahedral centre; the cited best aromatic products themselves have none detected.

The enriched N-halo and N-amino families lack consistently ordinary nitrogen attachment environments. The trajectories do not identify a particular unseen substituent that would improve the score.

Neither total aromaticity nor a specific halogen explains it.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
